description: A rate curve for the release-timing policies, because the 26% saving the paper quotes was measured at a single load point and a single point cannot tell a large effect near saturation from a modest one in the linear regime. Same policies and harness as e40; the only change is that rate is swept.
note_holdout: seed 99 and these rates were NOT used to fit the cost model — the fit came from e02's concurrency sweep at fixed n. plan_v4 requires MAPE<15% per cell on data the fit never saw.
note_rate_curve: 10 through 70 req/s. o5's throughput sweep put the knee for a 3000-token prompt between 8 and 12 req/s, but this workload is prompt_len=512, output_len=1, so its knee is elsewhere and the range is chosen to bracket rather than to assume it. The curve is the result; a single rate is what this experiment exists to replace.
note_harness_overhead: The known confound, restated because it bounds what this curve can say: e40's driver scrapes /metrics around every batch and adds a median 22.6-24.9 ms of inter-dispatch overhead on a policy that never waits. That inflates STOCK's p95 and therefore flatters any policy that deliberately delays, which is why the 'no detectable latency cost' reading of the 26% does not survive. The simulator models it as client_overhead_s; the hardware numbers here still carry it, so latency differences are lower bounds on the true cost of waiting.
